To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) 12 of the 23 MI proteins of Legionella pneumophilia were induced by prolonged inhibition of host cell macromolecular synthesis and were therefore artifacts, (ii) the 20-kDa inorganic pyrophosphate gene (ppa gene) ofL. pneumophilia was selectively induced during intracular infection, and (iii) the data indicate caution in long-term use of cyclohexamide treatment to selectively radiolable intracellular bacteria.

(i) cycloheximidine has no effect on intracellular bacterial replication, (ii) 23 MI genes of Legionella were identified, and (iii) one of the MI genes encodes a protein that may be involved in macromolecular biosynthetic capabilities of L. pneumophilia during intracellular infection.

the Legionella pneumophilia 20-kDa protein, which is induced during intracellular replication, is inorganic pyrophosphate and that the gene is regulated by a novel mechanism that is not dependent upon the presence of the intracellular environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms by which Legionella pneumophilagrown in the intracellular environment of the macrophages is able to survive and replicate in the macrophage cytoplasm.
the identification and cloning of genes of Legionella spp. that are induced during intracellular growth.
the molecular biology of Legionella pneumophilia, a facultative intracellular pathogen that causes Legionnaires' disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cycloheximideshould be used to selectively label intracellular bacteria for a maximum period of 6 h.
the use of cyclohexamide to selectively label intracellular bacteria should be used only in short-term experiments (i.e., less than 4 h).
the cycloheximidine treatment is not a suitable technique to study the gene expression by intracel-lular Legionella pneumophia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 20 kDa MI protein is an inorganic pyrophosphate which is induced by intracellular infection.
the Legionella pneumophilia gene encoding inorganic pyrophosphate (PPase) is induced during the intracellular phase of infection.

the Legionella pneumophilia 20-kDa protein is induced during intracellular growth and that the gene encoding this protein is the first example in L. pneumophilia of a gene that is selectively induced during the intracellular growth of L. pneumophilia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of cyclohexamide to label intracellular bacteria is fraught with potential problems.
inhibition of host cell biosynthesis for more than 6 h is not recommended for the selective radiolabeling of intracellular bacteria.

the long-term use (greater than or equal to12 h) of cyclohexamide to inhibit host cell protein synthesis has profound effects on the host cell, and it is not appropriate to assume that inhibition of host protein synthesis has only a selective effect on the intracellular bacteria.
